parts.label: (iii)
parts.answer: At $P$, $(x,y)=(2,3)$ and the normal has gradient $\frac32$. Thus $y-3=\frac32(x-2)$; setting $x=0$ gives $y=0$.
parts.official_mark_scheme_text: At $x=2$, $y=3$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=-\frac23$ — M1*; perpendicular gradient $=\frac32$ — M1*; line equation using their $(2,3)$ and their gradient — DM1; shows it passes through $(0,0)$ — A1 AG.
